evidence.quote: Earth has four primary jet streams: two polar jet streams, near the north and south poles, and two subtropical jet streams closer to the equator.

claims.statement: Earth has four primary jet streams: two polar and two subtropical.

evidence.quote: Jet streams are narrow bands of strong wind that generally blow from west to east all across the globe.
Earth’s four primary jet streams only travel from west to east.

claims.statement: Earth’s four primary jet streams generally travel from west to east across the globe.

evidence.quote: On average, jet streams move at about 110 miles per hour.

claims.statement: Jet streams move at about 110 miles per hour on average.

evidence.quote: But dramatic temperature differences between the warm and cool air masses can cause jet streams to move at much higher speeds — 250 miles per hour or faster.
Speeds this high usually happen in polar jet streams in the winter time.

claims.statement: Jet streams can move at 250 miles per hour or faster when temperature differences are dramatic, especially in polar jet streams during winter.

evidence.quote: Jet streams are located about five to nine miles above Earth’s surface in the mid to upper troposphere — the layer of Earth’s atmosphere where we live and breathe.

claims.statement: Jet streams are located about five to nine miles above Earth’s surface in the mid to upper troposphere.

evidence.quote: So, if an airplane flies in a powerful jet stream and they are traveling in the same direction, the airplane can get a boost.

claims.statement: An airplane flying in a powerful jet stream in the same direction can receive a boost.

evidence.quote: That’s why an airplane flying a route from west to east can generally make the trip faster than an airplane traveling the same route east to west.

claims.statement: A west-to-east airplane route can generally be completed faster than the same route traveled east to west.

evidence.quote: However, if a weather system is far away from a jet stream, it might stay in one place, causing heat waves or floods.

claims.statement: A weather system far from a jet stream might remain in one place, causing heat waves or floods.

evidence.quote: However, jet streams can move in different ways, creating bulges of winds to the north and south.

claims.statement: Jet streams can move in different ways and create northward and southward bulges of wind.

evidence.quote: Storms tend to follow the edge of the jet stream, where the difference between cool and warm air creates the turbulent conditions for storms.

claims.statement: Storms tend to follow the edge of the jet stream.
